Mention you work for The Independent to an American and, surprisingly often, they’ll ask if you know Trent Crimm. James Lance’s fictional sports journalist became one of the breakout stars of Ted Lasso, and for many American viewers, The Independent is no longer just a British newspaper — it’s the place where Trent Crimm files his columns.

Crimm’s popularity is a testament to just how deeply Ted Lasso embedded itself in the American cultural consciousness.

When the show first aired in 2020, it looked like an odd proposition: a sitcom spun out of a decade-old NBC Sports advert about an American football coach accidentally taking charge of an English Premier League club. Instead, it became one of Apple TV’s defining hits, winning 13 Emmy Awards across its first three seasons.

In 2023, it was the most-watched streaming original in the U.S. with 16.9 billion viewing minutes despite Apple TV’s smaller subscriber base. The show’s portrayal of masculinity and mental health also struck a chord. That same year, Sudeikis and the cast were invited to the White House by President Joe Biden to discuss mental health awareness, with the series praised for encouraging conversations around anxiety, vulnerability and asking for help.

Yet back in Britain, where the series is set, the reaction has always been a bit more... complicated.

open image in gallery The average American vs the average Brit watching ‘Ted Lasso’. (Jason Sudeikis and Tanya Reynolds in ‘Ted Lasso’ season four) ( Apple TV )

Plenty of British viewers love it, of course, but it has also attracted a level of eye-rolling rarely seen in the States.

To many, AFC Richmond is an impossibly sanitized version of English football, while Ted’s endless optimism grates against the nation’s dyed-in-the-wool cynicism. The show’s fourth season has only reopened that divide.

Why does a show about an American coaching an English football club resonate so differently across the Atlantic? We asked two Independent journalists who have each spent years living in both countries.

Tom: We don’t want anyone messing with our beautiful game

The moment I realized just how differently Americans viewed Ted Lasso came one Saturday morning in a soccer bar in Los Angeles, where I was living at the time.

The Premier League was on every screen. There were Liverpool shirts, Arsenal shirts, Manchester United shirts ... and AFC Richmond shirts, worn completely unironically.

open image in gallery Happy families: Jeremy Swift, Hannah Waddingham, Juno Temple and Jason Sudeikis in ‘Ted Lasso’ ( Apple TV )

I was aghast. No one laughed, or pointed at them behind their backs. They were treated the same as everyone else despite proudly wearing the colors of a football club that doesn’t actually exist.

To do this in the U.K. would invite an onslaught of mockery for the rest of your days.

For me, it summed up the difficulty many Brits have with Lasso: In the UK, we take our soccer seriously; it is our beautiful game. To wear the jersey of a fictional team cheapens something sacred. As the great Arsenal winger Robert Pires once said: “In England, football is a religion.”

Now, I’ll admit, I checked out of Ted Lasso after season one. Perhaps it gets drastically better and completely changes its DNA in the seasons I’ve missed, but somehow I doubt it. From what I’ve read, Ted Lasso is ultimately able to secure a top three finish for his club through the power of friendship and understanding.

But soccer is not this wholesome; it’s decades of emotional trauma punctuated by occasional moments of joy — depending on who you support.

Real managers aren’t given time to discover themselves; they’re sacked after six bad games. As Amazon’s All or Nothing documentary series has shown us, dressing rooms aren’t held together by homemade biscuits and heartfelt speeches. And fans don’t unite behind a common cause — they spend half their lives arguing with each other.

It feels especially jarring in the wake of the World Cup, which saw Fifa’s cartoon villain Gianni Infantino bow to the host nation’s attempts to Americanize the sport with “hydration breaks” (read: ad breaks) and a Super Bowl-style halftime show featuring Justin Bieber and — you guessed it — Sudeikis as Lasso!

That’s the irony at the heart of the show. Americans embraced Ted Lasso because it introduced them to English football. Many English fans struggle to embrace it because it feels like football reimagined through an American lens. It’s not the Premier League as we know it — it’s the Premier League as Americans wish it were.

open image in gallery In ‘Ted Lasso,’ even Hannah Waddingham’s intimidating club owner is quickly softened over the course of one season ( Apple TV+ )

Kevin: Ted Lasso was the right show at exactly the right moment

Ted Lasso arrived at a time when we all needed some cheering up. Deep in the pandemic-era doldrums of August 2020, the sweet-natured “soccer” manager with his avuncular mustache and a predilection for baking his own shortbread was a welcome force of positivity in the world.

For my (American) wife and me, the show felt tailor-made. We were both on the lookout for a feel-good, whimsical comedy to fill the post-Schitt’s Creek void in our lives, while I needed a stealthy way to indoctrinate her into the obsessive world of Premier League football addiction.

That tactic worked a dream, setting off a chain reaction that means she now gets independently furious about PSR restrictions and my team’s wantaway stars. As an unintended consequence, I have to hear about how hot Brett Goldstein is a little more often than I’d like, but that’s simply a cross I have to bear.

While British friends scoffed at the show’s setting, a sort of Richard Curtis-esque fantasia, I was charmed from afar. What Ted Lasso delivered was the promise of an easy watch that guaranteed an upbeat message and a happy ending, whether the team won or lost.

As much as I enjoyed the show, I have to admit I’m struggling to summon any excitement for the surprise fourth season that’s now upon us. Even by 2023, when the show initially ended its run, its overload of sweetness had begun to make my back teeth ache. Looking back, it now feels a part of the desperate optimism of the era that had us standing on doorsteps clapping for nurses.

open image in gallery ‘Like Trump, “Ted Lasso” might be proving it’s awkward when someone doesn’t know it’s time to get off the stage,’ writes Kevin EG Perry ( Getty )

America’s relationship to football has moved on too. We’ve just enjoyed a blockbuster World Cup where the country was exposed not to the watered-down sitcom version but the real thing in all its glory: shock results, the birth of genuine underdog heroes like Cape Verde keeper Vozinha and, perhaps most importantly of all, thousands upon thousands of real football fans sharing their passion for the sport, from the Norwegian hordes rowing through Miami to Scottish fans drinking Boston dry.

Ted Lasso was there too, but his appearance felt a little ill-judged. When Jason Sudeikis and Brendan Hunt turned up in character as Lasso and Coach Beard at the World Cup final, it was alongside Justin Bieber as part of FIFA’s bloated and much-maligned halftime show.

Ted Lasso has always been big on lessons, and later on, during the trophy presentation, President Trump offered one the show could do well to heed: It’s awkward when someone doesn’t know it’s time to get off the stage.

Walmart has revealed how it plans to deploy the nearly $3 billion in tariff refunds it received from the federal government.

During an earnings call, Chief Financial Officer John David Rainey said the company had collected “substantially all” of the $2.9 billion in refunds for which it was eligible.

The payout is the biggest publicly reported by a U.S. company since the federal government started returning tariff funds, following the Supreme Court’s February decision to strike down much of the president’s tariff authority, according to NewsNation. As of July, the government had issued roughly $100 billion in refunds.

For Walmart, much of that money is set to flow back to shoppers, executives have said.

“We've taken a disciplined approach to investing these funds back into customer experience and price leadership, prioritizing investment in grocery and general merchandise categories,” Rainey said on the Thursday call.

open image in gallery Walmart has revealed how it intends to use the nearly $3 billion in tariff refunds it has received from the federal government ( Getty Images )

“We're investing heavily in price because customers need us to,” CEO John Furner added. “Customers tell us they're still feeling some pressure.”

The company, the nation’s largest private employer, said that it rolled out more than 11,000 temporary price cuts in the U.S. during the second quarter — up from about 7,000 in the first.

Still, the burst of discounts arrives at a less-than-rosy moment for the retail behemoth.

Walmart’s comparable sales growth in U.S. stores came in at 2.6 percent, its smallest increase in over six years, according to The Wall Street Journal. By comparison, sales rose 4.1 percent in the first quarter.

The market did not greet the numbers warmly: Walmart shares fell 9 percent Thursday and are now down more than 20 percent from their May high, according to NBC News.

open image in gallery In May, Walmart warned that it might be forced to raise prices as fuel costs climbed ( Getty Images )

Company executives attributed some of the sales slowdown to rising fuel costs amid the ongoing war in Iran.

“As you go through month-by-month in the last quarter, you can tell when fuel prices increase and got above $4, and perhaps there's a psychological impact to that, that there are choices that consumers are making,” Rainey said.

In May, Walmart warned that it might be forced to raise prices as fuel costs climbed.

Walmart’s vast reach makes it a closely watched indicator of consumer spending: the company says more than 150 million customers visit its website or stores every week.

According to a recent Financial Times survey, a majority of Americans, 53 percent, believe their current financial situation is worse than it was at the end of Joe Biden’s presidency.

This year’s El Niño weather event could be the “strongest in a lifetime,” weather experts have warned

That's due to unusually warm sea surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean. This natural climate pattern occurs when east-to-west trade winds weaken, allowing warm water to shift eastward.

This is what fuels more storms and clouds over the region that can cause ripple effects through the global atmosphere - and the U.S. is no exception.

But AccuWeather Lead Long-Range Meteorologist Paul Pastelok said whether this El Niño breaks records or not, "it is about the impacts and the impacts will not change either way.”

open image in gallery The 2026-2027 El Niño climate pattern is expected to be very strong and potentially the strongest ‘in a lifetime,’ forecasters warn. That could mean more extreme weather impacts across America ( Getty Images )

The El Niño is already impacting weather in the U.S., stymying this year’s Atlantic hurricane production.

Expected to last through next year, the pattern should bring lingering heat through the fall months in northern and eastern states.

And it’s projected to send drenching storms across the southern swath of the country while the Atlantic stays quiet.

During the winter, El Niño could bring snow, sleet and freezing rain to the Southeast and southern Plains.

And Florida could see more thunderstorms than usual, while other parts of the Gulf Coast see less, according to CNN meteorologist Mary Gilbert.

Unfortunately, after the worst spring drought on record, any resulting snowpack is anticipated to provide little relief for the West’s decades-long water crisis.

“Even one big year is not going to save us,” John Berggren, a policy manager at environmental nonprofit Western Resource Advocates, told WIRED. “It might be a sigh of relief, but we'll be right back in it.”

Next year’s forecast is murkier, but temperatures could soar, and federal forecasters said last week that there is a 90 percent chance the 2026-2027 El Niño will reach the highest strength level.

There are four different strength levels, ranging from “weak” to “very strong.”

El Niño is the warm phase of the climate pattern known as the El Niño Southern Oscillation, which regulates global climate. These events occur every 2-7 years.

open image in gallery The El Nino pattern is the warm phase of the climate pattern known as the El Nino Southern Oscillation. It brings wetter weather in the southern states and warmer and drier conditions up north ( NOAA )

The last time the El Niño was this strong was in 1877, when a global famine killed more than 50 million people.

“Simultaneous multiyear droughts similar to those in the 1870s could happen again,” Deepti Singh, an associate professor at Washington State University, told The Washington Post in May.

“What is different now is that our atmosphere and oceans are substantially warmer than they were in the 1870s, which means the associated extremes could be more extreme,” she said.

How much human-caused climate change plays a role here is an ongoing debate.

But it’s clear that there are higher temperatures and stronger storms now due to climate change. This past July was the warmest on record.

“What we’ll see in 2027 is a sneak peek of what the new normal will be in 2035,” Zeke Hausfather, a climate scientist at Berkeley Earth, a nonprofit research organization, told The New York Times. “We’ll see things that have never happened before in our history in terms of temperature, drought conditions, extreme heat.”

In the summer of 1993, Manchester United won the title and then signed Roy Keane in a British record transfer. In 2001, United won the title and then bought Ruud van Nistelrooy. In 2008, the summer after winning the Premier League and Champions League, they signed Dimitar Berbatov not because they really needed him but because they could.

Each time, Alex Ferguson took steps not just to maintain the gap to their rivals but to grow it. Each time, United defended their Premier League crown.

Even before kick-off here at the Emirates Stadium, there was that familiar sense of a title-winning manager screwing down the lid on the Premier League trophy they owned. Mikel Arteta’s newest signing, Ezri Konsa, was paraded on the pitch to a standing ovation – quite the flex to sign the second best right-sided centre-half in the Premier League while the best, William Saliba, is sidelined with injury.

And after a few minutes of this opening 3-0 win over Coventry City, it was clear that Arteta had strengthened his attack too. Christos Tzolis impressed in pre-season games and topped most of Arsenal’s fitness metrics. Here he buzzed into action on the left wing, legs whirring with the urgency of a man fleeing a swarm of bees, all fast-twitch jolts and excitable energy, exactly the sort of opponent Coventry’s right-back Milan van Ewijk didn’t want to face on his first Friday night live on Sky Sports.

Arsenal had a plethora of attacking options on the field: Kai Havertz led the line, Bukayo Saka started on the right and Martin Odegaard flitted in and out of the right half-space. But for all the passing lanes on offer, the gameplan became a simple one: when in the final third, seek Tzolis.

open image in gallery Christos Tzolis sprints down the wing during Arsenal's win over Coventry ( AP )

The Greek loitered on the left touchline patiently waiting for a pass, and then he was off, surging towards the box, feinting left and right, dropping his shoulder and shifting his marker off-balance before exploiting the space he’d created. There were no stepovers or needless touches, just concise and efficient wing play, and it was devastatingly effective.

Tzolis had a hand in Arsenal’s first goal when his diligent press won the ball high up the pitch, before Riccardo Calafiori crossed for Havertz to sweep home. Four minutes later Tzolis turned creator with a low, left-footed cross which Coventry goalkeeper Carl Rushworth could only tip into the path of Saka, who knocked the ball into a half-empty net. It may not register as an official assist, like his two in the Community Shield last weekend, but there were plenty of signs that Tzolis will rack up productive numbers playing for his new team.

“I love this kind of energy every time he’s on the ball,” Arteta said. “I think he’s earned [the fans’ appreciation]. I think the way he has performed in the last few games has been phenomenal. What he transmits as a player, so direct, so incisive, constantly he wants to make things happen, and he has an incredible variety of actions in the last 30 metres to decide and to make the right decisions, even when the spaces are sometimes really, really small.”

open image in gallery Christos Tzolis and Cristhian Mosquera applaud the Arsenal fans ( PA )

Coincidentally, Tzolis made his Premier League debut in this stadium five years ago during a loan spell at Norwich City. It was a period of harsh learning in which his manager, Daniel Farke, hailed Tzolis as one of the brightest young players in Europe, but later publicly berated him for taking and missing a penalty at Anfield despite not being the manager’s designated penalty taker. Tzolis admitted his confidence was shot by the end of a move in which he made only six starts.

His breakthrough came during another loan at German side Fortuna Dusseldorf, and his performances earned him his move to Club Brugge two years ago. The last campaign was one of abundance for Brugge before this summer’s £34m switch to Arsenal, in which he scored 20 goals and recorded 29 assists. Brugge won the title and Tzolis was awarded Belgium’s player of the season.

Since that ill-fated spell at Norwich, Tzolis has recorded 122 goal contributions in 145 games. Even accounting for a career spent largely outside the big-five leagues, they are astonishing numbers.

open image in gallery Tzolis cuts inside and lets fly during the first half ( Getty )

It remains to be seen what competition Tzolis faces for his place at the Emirates. Arsenal’s very public pursuit of Vinicius Jr ultimately failed but would have immediately relegated Tzolis to understudy. Gabriel Martinelli was not in the Arsenal squad here despite being fit to play, and while the Brazilian’s ostracism secures Tzolis’s place in the short-term, it might suggest Arteta wants another new wide player. Juventus’s Kenan Yildiz remains a transfer target.

But Tzolis owns the left forward spot right now, and his task is to make himself undroppable no matter the competition. His determination to score was clear, taking a match-high four shots, none of which went particularly close. He may well end up setting new records for cutting inside and letting fly, which teammates won’t always thank him for. Calafiori may question his life choices when his fifth lung-bursting underlap is ignored.

But Tzolis’s track record suggests he could be the remedy to Arsenal’s limitation last season, in games against stubborn defences when they lacked the type of player to unlock the door. It is only one game of a long season, but there is a sense at the Emirates that Arteta has already begun work tightening Arsenal’s grip.

News.title: By calling out Natalie Harp, Jon Ossoff did what no Democrat has been able to do — put Trump on his heels
News.content:

Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

The past week, President Donald Trump has had to respond to and tamp down stories about Natalie Harp, his super-eager executive assistant who calls herself the “human printer.”

On Thursday evening, Trump biographer Michael Wolff released letters to The Daily Beast wherein Harp gushed to the president, “You are all that matters to me” and “no one knows or cares about me more.” The New York Times’ Maggie Haberman, perhaps the premier chronicler of Trump, has said Harp is “not beloved” by her colleagues in the White House.

Her estranged brother Preston burst out laughing on CNN the past week when he learned that his sister reportedly jumped into the trunk of a Trump motorcade SUV when there wasn’t room for her to sit during a trip to court in 2023. Then there was the story on MS NOW that Harp worked at the White House without a security clearance. On Thursday, First Lady Melania Trump made her first public appearance in a month amid reports she has refused to be anywhere Harp is, leading to her having a lower public profile of late.

“I heard you missed me,” she joked in her opening remark before adding, “Here I am.”

And all of this snowballed thanks to Sen. Jon Ossoff, the freshman Democrat from Georgia, who has become public enemy number one of the White House and plenty of other conservatives — merely for invoking Harp. And in doing so, he might have honed a skill Trump uses to maximum effect: occupying everyone’s attention and getting his opponents on the back foot.

open image in gallery Sen. Jon Ossoff caused a firestorm in Washington with his comments about White House executive assistant Natalie Harp. ( AFP/Getty )

Last week, Ossoff held a rally in Atlanta. These events have become something of an exhibition match for the 39-year-old senator who often clips videos from his re-election events that become catnip for liberals on social media.

The videos have generated talk not just about whether Ossoff will win by double digits this November, but whether he should seek the presidency in 2028.

This time, Ossoff rattled off an attack regarding the report that Trump left Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and the White House press pool on one plane as he faced a potentially deadly Iranian missile attack while he and Harp went on another plane.

“He golfs and trades stocks. See, he doesn’t want to do his job,” he said. “He wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace gifted by the Emir of Qatar.”

The line earned Ossoff applause in Georgia, but it earned him consternation from plenty of Republicans. Scott Jennings, the conservative CNN pundit who is reportedly lobbying to replace departing Karoline Leavitt as White House press secretary, called Ossoff a “garbage human.”

And the response from the White House was even more vicious. White House Communications Director Steven Cheung called Ossoff “Jon J***off” and a “cuck,” and spokesman Davis Ingle called him “cringeworthy, feminine theatre kid cosplaying as Barack Obama.” Trump for his part calls Ossoff “Pee-Wee Herman.”

Even some Democrats, like former Obama adviser David Axelrod, chafed at the attack.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump’s administration has been on the defensive about his relationship with Natalie Harp ever since Ossoff’s attack. ( Getty )

But to borrow a phrase regularly used in the South, a hit dog will holler. Ossoff’s attacks would not have caused such a stir if he did not know it would make the White House lash out at him.

Unlike some other Democrats, Ossoff, who represents a state that voted for Trump twice, has made opposing the GOP standard bearer a cornerstone of his re-election campaign.

His record is not as liberal as his MS NOW-watching fans might want. He voted for the Laken Riley Act, which would allow for immigration authorities to detain non-citizens arrested for or chanrged with specific crimes. He also voted to confirm Marco Rubio to be secretary of State and for Trump’s crypto legislation.

Still, he has bet that Trump’s sinking approval rating due to the poor economy and the war in Iran will juice up turnout in the midterm election against his ultra-MAGA challenger Rep. Mike Collins. Even when Trump won Georgia, suburban voters in the Atlanta metropolitan area trended leftward.

He likely hopes to dominate his re-election campaign and shake off the image he has as an upstart amateur who narrowly lost a special election congressional race in 2017. And of course, as much as he says he is not thinking about the White House, he is a senator from a swing state. And South Carolina, home of Democrats’ first primary contest, is just a quick drive away.

Ossoff has lapped up the attention and expect him to post a massive fundraising number. Whether due to his age, the voters in his state or something else, he might be the only Democrat who has figured out how to turn Trump’s best weapon–media attention–against him.

Rory McIlroy headed straight to the driving range after dropping off the pace during the BMW Championship's second round in St Louis.

The Masters champion opened with a six-under-par round to share the lead, but managed to improve his score by only a single stroke on Friday with a 69.

"I feel like conditions were pretty similar to yesterday," McIlroy told the Golf Channel.

"The wind was coming out of a different direction, but still very scorable. The greens are soft, maybe the ball’s got a little bit more run out on the fairways, but you’ll still see guys shooting pretty good scores today.

"I didn’t quite hit it as good as I did yesterday, so probably an afternoon on the range for me.

open image in gallery JJ Spaun impressed on Friday ( PA )

"I’m proud of how I just hung in there. A lot of good par putts on the back nine, especially. The only bogey I had was with a mistake on the par-five eighth hole, but I made some really good par saves coming in and that sort of kept me in it."

McIlroy’s underwhelming round came after Bryson DeChambeau hit back at the Northern Irishman after he questioned the value that the American and Jon Rahm had brought to LIV Golf, amid the breakaway league’s struggles.

DeChambeau said: "I think we just have a bit of a responsibility to continue to show this. If it works, it works; awesome. If it doesn’t, we’ll figure things out."

He added: "Time will move on, and I would say that time heals things. I hope people can see that we actually bring value to the game of golf. My wish is that people give us one more shot and be open minded."

American JJ Spaun looked on course to dominate the second round after reaching 11 under at the turn.

Three bogeys on the back nine slowed his advance, but two birdies, including at the 18th, set the early clubhouse target on 10 under.

World number one Scottie Scheffler, two over after a first-round 72, bogeyed the first but bounced back with five back-nine birdies to remain contending at three under.

News.title: Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

Full team news as and when we get it.

News.title: Russell takes Dutch GP sprint pole as Antonelli struggles to fifth
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for sprint qualifying for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix from Zandvoort. This is the last time the race will be on the F1 calendar for the foreseeable future, having been reintroduced in 2021 after a 35-year absence. It will be a shame to see it leave again, but never rule out it coming back, especially with Max Verstappen signing a lengthy contract extension with Red Bull.

What of the competitive action this weekend? As it is a sprint weekend, there is not a lot of preparation time, with just one practice session before sprint qualifying. In that it was a fairly close fight at the top, and it was Kimi Antonelli, the championship leader, who was fastest of all. Behind him was the McLaren of Lando Norris who was 0.121sec adrift then George Russell, who will be looking to kickstart his title campaign here, a further 0.004sec behind him.

Then came the two Ferraris of Lewis Hamilton (0.190sec) and Charles Leclerc (0.289sec) before a fairly significant gap of 0.659sec to Oscar Piastri in sixth. Verstappen was down in 11th, nearly 1.4sec off Antonelli’s ultimate pace but 0.5sec or so ahead of new (and old) team-mate for the weekend, Liam Lawson.

It was a tricky session for the drivers, though, as it began damp on a showery and blustery day by the Dutch seaside. Several drivers ran wide and off the track, though they all avoided anything more serious than gravel rash. The rest of the day looks to be drier but there are still a few showers around and the wind is all over the place, as it often is here.

Sprint qualifying starts at 3.30pm BST and we will be here for all of the updates for the nearly hour-long session.

News.title: Root delivers perfect riposte to captaincy doubters as England hammer Pakistan
News.content:
There was no attempt to be a Ben Stokes tribute act by Joe Root, just a measured captaincy performance very much in his own undemonstrative style.

Root, ever the team man, pushed his bowlers forward to lead England off at the end, recognising the match-winners in a walkover against Pakistan, who were bowled out for 135 in under two sessions.

Victory by an innings and 103 runs inside three days marked a perfect return to the job and put the smile back on England faces for the first time in a long while. The chants of “F--- the ECB” from Trent Bridge, after the New Zealand regime-toppling loss, were replaced by the Yorkshire faithful’s “Roooot”.

There was plenty of scepticism around rebooting the Root captaincy, but he was the only realistic choice. Harry Brook’s batting here was more sensible and at a tempo in the captain’s mould. “He is still learning the art of Test cricket,” Root said. Thrusting Brook into the job would have put more pressure on him, he may well have felt he needed to make risky statements with the bat. Now he can mature under Root and Stephen Fleming.

Tactically, Root was astute and showed enough to suggest he is going to be different this time. The old Root would not have whipped Jofra Archer off after two overs of the Test, but it was a prod that worked as he bowled quicker and more accurately to strike twice with the second-innings new ball, using his new-found skills with a scrambled seam to good effect.

It also showed his bowlers he wanted a fuller length and, from that first hour, they controlled the match and did not let their grip slip.

Root promised to keep the good aspects of Bazball and apply common sense. He continued Stokes’s leg-slip tactic and it paid off with the wicket of opener Azan Awais, and urged Ollie Robinson to bowl with the keeper standing up. England batted at 4.5 an over – a touch quicker than the Bazball years – but it was never reckless, just a calm tempo, with no ramps or scoops.

News.title: Officials selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers
News.content:
Officials in Malawi are selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers for around $20 and sending them on their way, a Telegraph investigation has found.



The passport-sized, yellow document, officially called the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP), is supposed to provide proof of vaccination against yellow fever, a mosquito-borne virus that kills tens of thousands of people every year.

The jab provides lifelong protection, beginning 10 days after vaccination. Most countries in Africa and Latin America require them for entry, either for all travellers or for those arriving from risk areas.



Yet travellers leaving Malawi through two major airports can get hold of the certificates without ever being vaccinated, according to interviews with multiple travellers and an undercover investigation.



Several passengers who travelled recently from Malawi to destinations including Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and China said they had obtained yellow fever vaccination certificates at airports or public hospitals without receiving the vaccine.



One traveller, who recently flew to Uganda for work from Kamuzu International Airport, which serves the capital, Lilongwe, said he was initially told it was too late to get vaccinated because his departure was less than 10 days away.



“When I asked the health officials if I could get vaccinated at the airport, I was told it was too late because I needed to be vaccinated ten days before my trip,” he told The Telegraph.



“But then they offered to arrange the certificate for me for roughly $21,” said the traveller, who asked not to be named. “I had to pay because I could not postpone the trip.”

News.title: Congo gambles on ‘old’ vaccine as new Ebola virus spirals
News.content:
Nearly half of all those infected have gone on to die.

Dr Sania Nishtar, chief executive of the Gavi global vaccine partnership, earlier this week said to beat the outbreak “we must deploy every tool at our disposal”.

She went on: “To avoid this becoming the worst recorded Ebola outbreak in history, it is critical that all effective countermeasure options are brought to bear.

“We have a tool that could help save lives while we wait for [Bundibugyo]-specific vaccines to become available.”

Previous clinical trials have shown that Ervebo is safe, but its effect on other strains is unknown.

The World Health Organisation said in a statement that while it was not known if Ervebo may protect against the Bundibugyo virus, “early laboratory and animal data suggest it may provide some protection”.

Medics told the Telegraph of anecdotal claims that health workers who had been given Ervebo to protect them during an outbreak of the Zaire strain in 2018 to 2020 had not fallen ill during the current Bundibugyo outbreak.

Health workers are at extreme risk of catching the disease because they come into contact with highly-contagious blood, vomit and diarrhoea from dying patients. When they fall sick themselves, they frequently go on to infect their own families.

Giving health workers vaccine jabs to protect them as they tend the sick is a cornerstone of Ebola responses.

The WHO said the vaccine allocation includes 20,000 doses for a Phase 3 clinical trial to understand the impact of the vaccine on the Bundibugyo virus. The remaining 50,000 doses will be used for front-line and health workers as recommended by WHO experts.

Dr Nishtar said: “Having already been licensed for the Zaire strain, we know that Ervebo is proven to be safe.

“And while the signs are that it may not stop transmission – which is essential for ending the outbreak - it could well save precious lives and reduce suffering.”

Health officials warn that the Bundibugyo outbreak centred on DRC’s Ituri province is easily outpacing relief efforts.

The virus is thought to have been spreading for months before an outbreak was finally declared in mid-May and medics have been unable to make up the head start.

An analysis by the Africa Centres for Disease Control meanwhile warned the current outbreak dwarfed all others on record

The current outbreak had almost ten times more cases than any other previous outbreak at a similar stage.

News.title: Soaring welfare bill pushes national debt to almost £3tn
News.content:
Britain’s soaring welfare bill forced John Healey to borrow more to balance the books last month.

The gap between tax receipts and spending unexpectedly resulted in a £1.8bn deficit in July, taking the national debt to within a whisker of £3tn.

Economists had predicted the Government would borrow nothing and blamed the deficit on the rising welfare bill.

Figures published by the Office for National Statistics (ONS) this morning show total debt rose to £2.985tn in July.

Benefit payments also climbed by 7.2pc, or £2bn, to £30bn last month.

The Chancellor now faces another tax-raising Budget in October, even as strong receipts from self-employed workers provide some respite.

The ONS also said Mr Healey spent £7.7bn on debt interest in July alone, almost 10pc higher than a year ago.

Ashley Webb, at Capital Economics said: “The weak performance was mainly due higher social payments.”

Monthly borrowing was slightly higher than the Office for Budget Responsibility and markets expected, meaning the Government has borrowed £56.7bn this financial year to plug the gap between tax receipts and public spending.

Julian Jessop, an independent economist and IEA economics fellow, said: “The latest official data highlight the fragility of the public finances as John Healey prepares his first Budget. Government borrowing was £2.3bn above forecast in July, and £0.7bn higher than in the same month a year ago.”

July is traditionally a strong month for receipts from the self-employed, with self-assessed income tax receipts last month coming to £17.1bn, about £1.7bn more than a year earlier.

However, higher inflation triggered by the Iran war means Mr Healey will be forced to use the Budget to find billions of pounds to repair the public finances.

Mr Healey said: “Fiscal discipline is the bedrock of our UK economic stability and national security which is why we are committed to meeting our fiscal rules, with a buffer against global uncertainties.”

The Resolution Foundation warned that the Chancellor’s headroom against his fiscal rules - self-imposed guardrails to guide public spending - has shrunk from around £24bn in the Spring Statement to less than £8bn today.

The think tank called on the Chancellor to use his first Budget on Oct 28 to put the nation’s finances on a more sustainable path.

Elliott Christensen, senior economist at the Resolution Foundation, said: “The Chancellor’s margin against his fiscal rules is now razor thin.”

News.title: Brook falls agonisingly short of Headingley hundred again as England continue to dominate
News.content:
“Yeah, of course I did,” said Cox, when asked if he was frustrated to miss out on three figures. Cox was caught behind off spinner Ali Usman, but believed he had hit his pad with his bat, not the ball.

“Once I got to fifty, I moved to sixty quickly, and thought ‘there’s a chance here’. Just keep being disciplined, ball by ball. I had it at the back of my mind, thinking you have worked so hard, do not give this opportunity up. That is exactly what I do in county cricket. I get to fifty, see how many runs I need to score, and work down from there.”

Asked if his team-mates were feeling the same emotion, he said: “Oh yeah there is. Every team, every player wants to score Test hundreds. Four of us got fifties, so we were hoping one would kick on, and instead of making it just a hundred, make it 150 or 170.

“I am thrilled. I would have taken it at the start of the Test match. I let myself down a tiny bit, but at the end of the day, you take 70.”

Cox resumed on day two on 23, then was dropped by the bowler Khurram Shahzad on 57. In the course of his innings, he was compared to AB de Villiers by the former England captain Michael Vaughan.

Cox is likely to get a good run across formats. England had hoped to call on Sam Curran for the third Test of this series, but his summer is over due to a groin injury. Curran will undergo surgery on Friday.

It is likely England will be without Curran, Bethell and Tom Banton for September’s white-ball series against Sri Lanka, which should mean greater opportunity for the likes of Cox and Sussex’s James Coles, and could even see a recall for Zak Crawley, who made an assured 81 for Kent against Middlesex on Thursday. Will Jacks is currently sidelined with appendicitis, but is expected to have recovered in time for the series.

Sports.title: Martin Odegaard responds to cheeky dig from Sky Sports host - 'Thanks for reminding me'
Sports.content:
Martin Odegaard responds to cheeky dig from Sky Sports host - 'Thanks for reminding me'

Martin Odegaard continued his fine start to the season and the Arsenal ace saw the funny side when he was reminded that he's already scored more goals than last season

View 2 Images Martin Odegaard was reminded that he only scored once last season - but saw the funny side (Image: Sky Sports)

Martin Odegaard was able to see the funny side after Sky Sports anchor Dave Jones reminded the Arsenal ace that he's already surpassed his goal tally from last season.

‌



The Norwegian scored the Gunners' third as they made light work of Coventry on Friday night. It is the team's second 3-0 win inside six days having also beat Manchester City in the Community Shield last Sunday by the same scoreline.

‌



Odegaard was also on target in Cardiff, meaning his two goals so far this season have outdone the one he scored last season. The Arsenal captain was made aware of that on Sky Sports, prompting him to respond: "Thanks for reminding me".

‌



Odegaard's strike in the second-half was a scuffed effort, but was still able to make it past Carl Rushworth in the Coventry goal. "Top finish I would say," he said sarcastically with a smile.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Last season the Norwegian's only goal came in a 2-1 win over Brighton at the Emirates, but on Friday he was named the Player of the Match as he excelled. Odegaard accepts that last season he struggled to replicate the level he's shown in previous years, but feels he's primed to find top gear once again.

‌



He said: "I think last season was a big struggle for me, lots of injuries and weird situations with bad luck. Could never find the rhythm, it is hard when you go in and out and sometimes you're maybe playing not at 100 per cent.

"It was hard, but I feel good now, my body is good. I had a good summer, a good World Cup and a good pre-season. Now I'm feeling 100 per cent and that always helps."

View 2 Images The Norwegian scored Arsenal's third against Coventry

‌



Arsenal's win was the perfect start to the defence of their title. Only three teams have ever gone back-to-back in the Premier League, but Odegaard insists that's the aim.

"For sure that's the mindset," he said. "We don't feel we have to defend anything. We want to do it again and that's the mindset. Last year is finished now, we want to do it again and we want to attack it and fight for it again.

"The perfect start. It's always good to start with a win. A win at home, three goals and a clean sheet. It was really solid."

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi issues honest message to Tottenham stars as he justifies transfer spend
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi issues honest message to Tottenham stars as he justifies transfer spend

Tottenham have spent north of £300million this summer, breaking their transfer record under Roberto De Zerbi, and the Italian is adamant players have to be ready for the competition within the squad

View 2 Images Roberto De Zerbi has spoken about Tottenham's huge summer spend

Roberto De Zerbi has told Tottenham’s players they can leave if they are unhappy after the club’s £300million-plus summer spending spree.

‌



Tottenham are closing in on an £85m deal for Brazilian winger Savinho and are also set to sign his Manchester City teammate Omar Marmoush.

‌



They have broken the £100m barrier to sign Italy star Sandro Tonali and spent big on Jan Paul van Hecke and Mateus Fernandes. But it will turn up the competition for places with the likes of Richarlison and Pape Matar Sarr unlikely to be regular starters.

‌



Spurs boss De Zerbi, though, insisted the club had to spend big after two successive 17th place finishes and flirtations with relegation. De Zerbi said: “I love speaking clearly. Today is August 21st, I think every one of those players, they already know the squad. If one of them doesn’t want to accept the competition inside the pitch, inside the dressing room, they can leave.

“I try to be honest and to make the better decision I can on the pitch to find the best first XI. But the players have to accept why because if we want to become better, if we want to compete for the top of the table, 11 players are not enough, 15 players are not enough.

‌



“If you analyse the teams Liverpool two years ago, Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester City, Bayern Munich, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Juventus, Milan, the squad there is a big competition inside the dressing room.

Sports.title: Arsenal hammer Coventry to send ominous message to Premier League rivals - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Arsenal hammer Coventry to send ominous message to Premier League rivals - 5 talking points

ARSENAL 3-0 COVENTRY CITY: The champions sent out an ominous message to their Premier League rivals as the likes of Kai Havertz and Bukayo Saka scored in a rampant win

View 4 Images Arsenal made light work of Coventry to begin their season with three points

Arsenal made light work of newly promoted Coventry as the champions began the defence of their title with minimal fuss to go top of the table.

‌



The Gunners were handed the chance to kick off the season and needed only a quarter of an hour to score the first Premier League goal of 2026/27 as Kai Havertz got the ball rolling at the Emirates.

‌



The German, who only started seven league games last term as injuries plagued him, was able to sweep home first time after being found by Riccardo Calafiori, who seized on a Coventry error.

‌



Arsenal's second came just seven minutes later as Bukayo Saka was able to tap into an empty net from seven yards. Coventry were outclassed throughout and it would take them 85 minutes before they registered an effort on target.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The hosts only needed three minutes of the second-half to score their third as Saka and Ben White teamed up down the right to eventually find Martin Odegaard, whose scuffed shot was still enough to beat Carl Rushworth, who should've done better.

‌



Coventry were able to prevent the floodgates opening as they kept Arsenal scoreless for the final 40 minutes in the capital, even if they offered nothing in attack. Easier assignments await, starting next week against Hull, whilst the Gunners know tougher tests are to come.

Here's five talking points from the Emirates.

Arsenal irresistible

It is easy to say they were playing a newly promoted team, but Arsenal wore their champion tag with a real swagger. It is the first time since 2004 that the Gunners began the year as the Premier League's premier club - on that occasion they hammered Everton 4-1.

‌



View 4 Images Bukayo Saka doubled Arsenal's lead in the first-half

22 years on and they looked equally as impressive, taking control from minute one and sending an ominous message to the rest of the league. Tougher tests are of course to come, but Arsenal could not have hoped for better on opening night.

Coventry's tough first day

They say every day is a school day, and the Premier League new boys were dealt a tough lesson. They claimed the Championship title last term but after only 22 minutes in north London were two goals down and, effectively, having to look to next week for their first hope of points.

‌



A clearance that was blocked ultimately led to Arsenal's opener, no doubt Milan van Ewijk will wonder why he didn't just boot the ball into Row Z. Most promoted teams often have to be on the receiving end of a one-sided encounter in the opening weeks to truly understand what they're up against - Coventry had theirs on day one.

View 4 Images Frank Lampard's Coventry were dominated from minute one in north London

Havertz takes the initiative

The German endured an injury-hit campaign last year but was straight back into the team once fit, scoring in the Champions League final. On Friday Havertz got the nod over Viktor Gyokeres, who was sat watching from the bench when he saw his team-mate sweep home the Arsenal opener on 15 minutes.

‌



A lot of the Arsenal questions have been answered, but the champions are seemingly still undecided over whether Havertz, a false 9, is the man who can take them to the next level ahead of a natural striker in Gyokeres. Goals will ultimately prove the biggest decider and Havertz has the starting berth, which he looks set to keep.

Odegaard's classy reminder

Once upon a time Odegaard was Arsenal's undisputed No 10, everything good about their attack ran through him. Then he sustained the odd injury and Arteta continued to invest in players who were capable of filling his playmaking role, and all of a sudden there's been questions over the Norwegian's future.

View 4 Images Martin Odegaard was central to Arsenal's attacking quality

‌



It almost felt as though the ex-Real Madrid star knew that people had raised the debate over whether he should command the start he did several years ago, but based on this performance few, if any, can argue that Odegaard remains one of the classiest operators in England, let alone Arsenal. Ironically his strike which saw him get on the scoresheet was perhaps his worst touch of the night, still, they all count.

MLS looks a stayer

Ever since the news broke that Myles Lewis-Skelly had been offered to Manchester United and Chelsea the versatile midfielder has been an ever present. Arteta insists he wants to keep the academy star and, despite the reports linking him with an exit, Lewis-Skelly looks every bit part of the fabric.

He played in the latter weeks of pre-season, started in the Community Shield win and played from the beginning against Coventry. Seeing him leave would no come as a massively surprise. The same though can't be said for Ethan Nwaneri.

Sports.title: Man United set for transfer windfall thanks to sell-on clause as player in 'advanced talks'
Sports.content:
Man United set for transfer windfall thanks to sell-on clause as player in 'advanced talks'

Manchester United's transfer funds could receive a boost before the end of the summer window as they benefit from a deal agreed in 2024

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's Man United transfer kitty could receive a boost (Image: Marc Atkins, Getty Images)

Manchester United are set to see their transfer funds boosted when Willy Kambwala finalises his departure from Villarreal. Kambwala, 21, is on course to join Italian side Como and United will cash in thanks to having the foresight to include a sell-on clause.

‌



Como are looking likely to pip Spanish club Osasuna to his signing and the Red Devils will pocket. United sources described the sell-on clause for Kambwala as "sizeable" when he departed the club two years ago after making his debut aged 19.

‌



However, Villarreal are only expected to take in a modest fee, limiting the amount that United will receive. Kambwala departed Old Trafford in 2024 when the Yellow Submarine came in for the player.

‌



Villarreal tabled an offer of €5.5million (£4.7m) plus €6m (£5.14m) in add-ons to acquire Kambwala from United. The agreement incorporated a buy-back option and matching rights for three years, alongside the sizeable sell-on clause.

United occasionally included clauses in player sales prior to Sir Jim Ratcliffe's investment in the club, but it has since become standard practice following Ineos taking charge of football operations It is now a crucial part of negotiations when players head out of the club.

United included a "high percentage" sell-on clause and buyback option in the sale of Tyler Fredricson to Lausanne-Sport, with comparable clauses also written into the sale of Radek Vitek to Middlesbrough.

‌



United inserted a buy-back clause into the deal with Boro, along with matching rights and a sell-on clause of up to 35 per cent to profit from any potential future sale. Ethan Williams was transferred to Peterborough last week, with United inserting a 50 per cent sell-on clause into the agreement, alongside a buyback option and matching rights clauses.

Ethan Ennis completed a permanent switch to Stockport County earlier this week. United included a 50 per cent sell-on clause in that deal, as well as buyback and matching rights clauses.

View 2 Images Willy Kambwala left Manchester United in 2024 (Image: Getty)

‌

United still hope to add to their squad before the end of the month. Michael Carrick is hopeful the club can take advantage of any opportunities in the final days of the transfer window.

"I just think we're looking to strengthen the squad," he said. "We're certainly working towards that, making the most of the situation that we have and trying to improve things and trying to move forward.

Sports.title: Arsenal transfer 'proof' revealed live on Sky Sports in Julian Alvarez and Vinicius Jr claim
Sports.content:
Arsenal transfer 'proof' revealed live on Sky Sports in Julian Alvarez and Vinicius Jr claim

Arsenal's transfer for Vinicius Junior ended in disappointment for Gunners fans, but there has been an interesting revelation during a broadcast live on Sky Sports

View 3 Images Ian Wright said he has 'proof' Vinicius Jr was signing for Arsenal

Sky Sports pundit Ian Wright has claimed he has "proof" Vinicius Junior was set to move to Arsenal this summer. The Gunners were engaged in a high profile transfer pursuit of the Brazilian, which ended with the forward signing a new contract at Real Madrid.

‌



It was a fascinating saga for football fans which saw plenty of toing-and-froing during the negotiations. With Vinicius' move now not happening, Arsenal are now pursuing Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez.

‌



However, as Wright briefly started speaking about the Argentinian, he insisted Vinicius was, at one stage, on his way to Arsenal, despite both Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher appearing unconvinced.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Neville asked a leading question about Vinicius to Wright at the start of Sky Sports pre-match coverage of their Premier League opener against Coventry City. After Neville said: "Who are they bringing in?" Wright replied: "This is what I am saying.

"They were talking about...I don't know if Alvarez is coming. Obviously, then went for Vini, I know that was happening, people laughed at me. You two laughed."

‌



After Carragher snapped back: "That was never happening" Wright then replied: "At some stage, Ill show you, I'll show you the proof."

View 3 Images Vini Jr remained at Real Madrid amid interest from Arsenal (Image: Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Wright did not divulge what exactly his proof was in regards to Vinicius, at one stage of the saga, heading to Arsenal this summer. He signed a new six-year deal to remain at the Bernabeu instead of moving to north London.

‌



Vinicius Jr was the second big name attacker to snub Arsenal, after Morgan Rogers opted to move to Chelsea for £117m. The Gunners have now switched their focus to Alvarez, which is proving to be another drawn out transfer saga.

Atletico did not include him in their La Liga opener against Malaga, after Diego Simeone stated the World Cup winner was not in the right frame of mind to compete.

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal pursued a move for Vinicius Jr (Image: 2026 The Arsenal Football Club Plc)

‌



After Wright told Carragher and Neville about his transfer "proof" he then added: "That's where we're going. I don't think we need to change the way we are playing, I just think we need to bring in that calibre of player to force it home."

One new signing who is already exciting Arsenal fans is Greek winger Christos Tzolis. His arrival from Club Brugge took place somewhat under the radar, as Arsenal were in the middle of the Vinicius and Rogers transfer sagas.

Sports.title: Chelsea secure agreement to host Champions League games for Shakhtar Donetsk
Sports.content:
Chelsea secure agreement to host Champions League games for Shakhtar Donetsk

Shakhtar Donetsk will play their home Champions League games at Stamford Bridge after striking a deal with Chelsea, who failed to qualify for Europe

View 2 Images Stamford Bridge will host Champions League football this season

Chelsea will host Champions League football this season after they agreed to let Shakhtar Donetsk play their home games at Stamford Bridge.

‌



The Ukrainian side have not played a match at their home stadium, the Donbas Arena, for more than 12 years due to the Russian invasion into Ukraine.

‌



As a result they've played across Europe with Shakhtar having to call the likes of Hamburg and Warsaw their temporary homes. Now they'll call London their home for a year and have settled on using Chelsea's ground having also considered playing at Brentford’s Gtech Stadium.

‌



Chelsea endured a poor year last season, going through two permanent managers, which meant they finished down in tenth and thus failed to qualify for any kind of European football.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

That has left Stamford Bridge free on Champions League nights and the Blues have decided to allow Shakhtar to play their home games in west London with the group stage draw still to be made.

‌



A Chelsea statement read: "FC Shakhtar have played in countries across Europe and we look forward to welcoming them to London for their Champions League campaign this year. We will be working with the Shakhtar team closely over the coming weeks to ensure that matchdays run safely and smoothly for their team and supporters."

Shakhtar have only played once at Stamford Bridge, that coming in November 2012 when they were undone by a last minute Victor Moses header in a five-goal thriller.

View 2 Images Shakhtar Donetsk's only outing at Stamford Bridge came back in 2012

‌



Shakhtar themselves have thanked the Premier League side for the opportunity. They said: "Playing our Champions League home matches at Stamford Bridge is a special opportunity for Shakhtar. We are grateful to Chelsea Football Club for the opportunity to host our games at this special venue. Stamford Bridge is one of the most famous stadiums in world football, with an incredible history and atmosphere. We are convinced that Shakhtar’s matches in London will provide unforgettable emotions for Ukrainian and English fans."

The Ukrainian side's best effort in the Champions League came back in 2011, when they made the quarter-finals. They topped a group that included Arsenal, beating the north Londoners at home, before Pep Guardiola's Barcelona ended their journey.

Sports.title: 'A massive 10 days' - Neville tells Arsenal to get Alvarez before deadline
Sports.content:
Defending Premier League champions Arsenal would become Champions League winners if they land Julian Alvarez in the final days of the transfer window, says Gary Neville.

The Gunners have made an impressive start to the new campaign, backing up their Community Shield win over Manchester City with a 3-0 demolition of newly-promoted Coventry.

However, Sky Sports pundit Neville says Arsenal still need "a bit of magic up front" and believes Atletico Madrid's Alvarez is the player who would deliver it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Arsenal and Coventry

Arsenal, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain are among the clubs keen on Argentina international Alvarez, although Atletico CEO Miguel Angel Gil said earlier this summer that they do not want to sell Alvarez and would not even accept £170m for the forward.

Neville has encouraged Arsenal to test Atletico's resolve in a bid to take themselves to the next level.

"What a squad [Mikel Arteta] has built," said Neville. "If he puts another forward into that, if they could get Julian Alvarez somehow, that would light this place up as you'd have a world-class striker to go with all the world-class defenders and midfielders.

"They wouldn't just become Premier League title winners they'd go the next step and win a Champions League. It's a massive 10 days. He needs a bit of magic up front - someone that can win a game for you when you don't play well."

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Arteta insisted "the main focus has to be to improve our players and the connection between them". He noted how little Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Ben White played together down the right flank last season due to injuries.

However, Neville reckons Odegaard would be even more destructive if he had a striker like Alvarez to target.

"He [Odegaard] is exceptional. If there was an Ian Wright-type player up front for Arsenal who makes those short runs he'd be even better," said Neville.

Image: Arsenal's Martin Odegaard celebrates scoring his side's third goal against Coventry

"As [Kai] Havertz and [Viktor] Gyokeres always come to the ball, Odegaard has to play possession rather than playing the slip passes. If Arsenal were to sign Julian Alvarez then he'd go up a level as it would be perfect for the style of play."

Fellow Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher agreed Arsenal still need something special in the attacking areas, although he reckons Odegaard and Saka are showing signs of being able to reach world-class levels.

"I still think Arsenal lack a world-class player in the front four," he said. "About two years ago I thought Saka and Odegaard would make that next step. For whatever reason it's not happened due to injuries or Arsenal not being at their best. Those two were close to getting to the levels shown by Man City and Liverpool players, like [Kevin] De Bruyne and [Erling] Haaland or [Mohamed] Salah and [Sadio] Mane. They took their teams to the title.

"Arsenal won the league without [Saka and Odegaard] doing it. They did it by having a great defence and goalkeeper. But I still think Saka and Odegaard can get back to where they were a couple of years ago."

Carragher added: "The psychological factor of being champions now will take this Arsenal team to another level rather than buying a superstar player."

Analysis: Odegaard and Tzolis rejuvenate Arsenal attack

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz at the Emirates Stadium:

Vinicius Jr this, Morgan Rogers that... Arsenal have shown that their transfer window was better than many made out.

Tzolis looks like a gem, a real livewire down the left wing. After a stale opening five minutes on the pitch, he set it alight with two shots and two chances created in the space of four minutes.

It was no surprise to se him strongly involved in the two goals that put this game to bed, winning the ball high up for the first, then crossing for Saka for the second.

But Odegaard's start to the season cannot be overlooked either. He backed up the stunning Community Shield display with a first goal of the season here, equalling his league tally last season that saw him miss 30 matches in all competitions.

In fact, this was just the second time since December 2024 that Saka, Odegaard and Havertz had started together. All three scored against Coventry.

Odegaard is like a new signing. And with three open-play goals, Arsenal look like a new team.

Sports.title: Arsenal kick off title defence with thumping win over Coventry
Sports.content:
Arsenal made a flying start to their Premier League title defence with a 3-0 thumping of newly-promoted Coventry City in the season opener at the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners showed their readiness to go again with an impressive demolition of Man City in the Community Shield last weekend and they sent another statement to their rivals for the crown with this demonstration of dominance.

Coventry's unwanted stat Coventry became the first team to have no touches in the opposition box or make a tackle in the first half of a Premier League game, since Opta started collecting that data in 2007.



They eventually made their first tackle on 69 minutes - when they were 3-0 down.

Once again new signing Christos Tzolis shone. The Greece international notched two assists at the Principality Stadium and was involved in Arsenal's first two goals on his Premier League debut, first winning the ball back for Riccardo Calafiori to tee up Kai Havertz and then sending in the cross Coventry 'keeper Carl Rushworth diverted into Bukayo Saka's path. "What a left-winger Arsenal have got," purred Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher on co-commentary.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kai Havertz fires Arsenal in front against Coventry as the Gunners begin their title defence

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bukayo Saka doubles Arsenal's lead

This was a reality check for Coventry on their return to the top flight after 25 years away. They failed to make a tackle in the first half - they could not get near Mikel Arteta's men. It did not get much better for them after the interval, with Martin Odegaard's miscued finish adding a third for Arsenal just four minutes into the second period.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Odegaard nets the third for Arsenal

With Ben White, Saka and Odegaard combining brilliantly through the right channel, Tzolis electric on the left, and Havertz looking sharp ahead of some slick midfield play from Declan Rice and Myles Lewis-Skelly, Arsenal already look up to speed and formidable.

Where was Guimaraes? New Arsenal midfielder Bruno Guimaraes was missing with a thigh injury he picked up in the Community Shield win over Man City.

Their defence was barely tested but Ezri Konsa's pre-match welcome, following his £55m move from Aston Villa, was a reminder they have brought even greater strength and depth to that department, too. Tougher tests are to come, with Aston Villa away and Chelsea at home next on the fixture list, but Arsenal are going to take some stopping.

Coventry, meanwhile, will be relieved they do not have to face Arsenal again until April. They host Hull City next weekend in a fixture which will carry far more significance for their season.

The key moments from the Emirates

5: SHOT! Tzolis shoots over after cutting inside from the left flank.

7: OVER! Saka's shot is deflected over after Tzolis pops up on the right.

8: CLOSE! Tzolis is involved in everything Arsenal do in attack but sends his second shot of the game over after a well-worked short corner.

9: OVER! Declan Rice shoots over from 25 yards as Arsenal make a fast start.

15: GOAL! Tzolis wins the ball off Milan van Ewijk deep in Coventry territory, Calafiori crosses low for Havertz and the striker sweeps in a fine finish to give the Gunners the lead.

23: GOAL! Rice and Odegaard combine in midfield and Saka is perfectly placed to tuck in when Tzolis' cross is diverted into his path by Coventry 'keeper Rushworth.

Image: Havertz celebrates scoring the opening goal with Saka

34: CHANCE! Arsenal work the ball into the Coventry box and White is onto it but sees his shot blocked away. Coventry scrambling.

43: SHOT! Loum Tchaouna's overhead kick from the edge of the box loops onto the roof of the Arsenal net.

45+1: CLOSE! Rice whips a shot beyond the far post after another short corner.

49: GOAL! Odegaard, Saka and White combine through the right channel before the captain's miscued shot deceives Rushworth and adds Arsenal's third.

Image: Odegaard celebrates his goal

53: SAVE! Rushworth tips a curling effort from Lewis-Skelly over the bar for a corner as Arsenal keep their pedal to the metal.

66: SHOT! Tzolis stings Rushworth's palms with a drive from the edge of the box from an Arsenal corner.

90: SAVE! Rushworth is at full stretch to prevent Havertz arrowing in a fourth after some neat footwork from the Arsenal striker.

Arteta: A lot to like and big individual performances

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to Sky Sports:

"There was a lot to like. We were really dominant and flowed with the ball, connecting well with one another. We should have scored more goals.

150 PL wins up for Arteta Mikel Arteta recorded his 150th Premier League victory in charge of Arsenal, and is now one of only five managers to reach 150 wins in fewer than 250 games (249), after Pep Guardiola (204), Jose Mourinho (231), Jurgen Klopp (237), and Alex Ferguson (247).

"Overall the performance was positive with some big individual performances.

"When you talk about connection and chemistry those three [Saka, Odegaard and White] have that. They play so many minutes together in the past but they didn't play much last year due to different situations. Even on the left side with Tzolis you are seeing different dynamics. I was really impressed."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Friday Night Football panel discuss whether Arsenal are still shy of a world-class attacker that would see them get over the line to win their first UEFA Champions League title

Arsenal playing with swagger?

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher:

"We'll know in a few weeks if there is a little bit of swagger about them or whether it was just the case they were playing against a team that were not used to that level. But Arsenal showed their class."

Odegaard: We can play even better!

Martin Odegaard speaking to Sky Sports:

"The first game is always a bit nervy. They played well, gave us a good fight and a good battle. Was key to get the first goal and control the game. It was solid.

"We looked good. We could have created and scored more. We can be more precise and sharp around the box. It's a good performance but we can do even better.

"The quality in the squad is unbelievable. You can put anyone on the pitch and they can perform at the highest level. We push one another to get better."

Lampard: A big learning curve

Coventry boss Frank Lampard:

"I didn't mind the reaction towards the end of the game as we went on. I saw some okay things there. It was a big learning curve, I believe they kept going, they kept going much to the end.

"There's Premier League debuts, there's noise here, I remember that [as a player]. It's different to the Championship in a way, no matter where you go.

"So those things are things to handle as a player, and we talked about a lot before the game. They'll have to go through that and experience that."

YOUR VIEWS: Coventry concerns and encouraging signs for Arsenal

Sheldon: Quality of Tzolis!! I know it's a first game back but if he continues like that £34m looks like a bargain, great first performance from the champions COYG!!

Reeze: Arsenal will walk the league this year, even without adding another forward. Problem is, they probably will add another!

Craig: Arsenal looked good and comfortable and never really had to break sweat but I thought Coventry were very, very poor, the goalkeeper has thrown one in and gifted them another. Tonight won't define their season but they are going to have to be much, much better.

Sports.title: Wigan top Super League table with win over Wakefield as Leigh rout Bradford
Sports.content:
Wigan eased to the top of the Betfred Super League table with a club-record 12th straight win after seeing off gutsy Wakefield 26-12 at the Brick Community Stadium.

Matt Peet's men brutally exploited a series of handling errors by the visitors to muscle into a 20-point half-time lead, then repelled a fine fightback with Jai Field's length-of-field interception just past the hour mark to seal their win.

The manner and timing of their move into pole position looks ominous for their top-flight rivals, not least long-time leaders Leeds who are now under pressure when they head to York on Sunday.

Peet praised his side's tenacity, saying: "I'm very pleased with how the game unfolded. The first half was intense and went set for set for a long time and we came out the other side of that.

"In the second half we got a little bit sloppy but we had to defend for the most part and it probably did us good. Wakefield throw so much threat at you and they never stop asking questions."

It marked a fourth straight loss for Wakefield, who started well and were aggrieved to be denied the opening try when Oliver Pratt sent Max Jowitt sliding over, but he was ruled to have knocked on in the process of grounding.

Moments earlier, Wakefield rode their luck to stay level after a rare error from Bevan French, who sent Zach Eckersley over in the corner from a forward pass.

Luke Thompson came close for Wigan while Wakefield continued to benefit on the short side as a high-quality contest moved past the quarter-hour without a point on the board.

But Wigan proceeded to capitalise on a pair of Wakefield errors to run in three tries in the next 10 minutes and give themselves an almost insurmountable advantage.

French ruthlessly punished a careless pass by Jowitt by powering over the halfway line to open the scoring, and six minutes later Wigan built on a penalty pass with Kian McDermott's superb ball gifting Liam Marshall the second in the corner.

Marshall was in for his second almost immediately after another handling error gifted Wigan the advantage. Three kicks from Adam Keighran - coupled with a penalty on the hooter - sent Peet's men in at the interval four scores to the good.

Wakefield might have been all but resigned to another defeat but they will take great heart from the way they refused to accept the seemingly inevitable at the start of the second half.

They seized on a sustained spell of pressure to narrow the deficit on 52 minutes when Jake Trueman's clever kick eluded French and gave Corey Hall the chance to touch down.

Trinity pushed again on the back of a penalty and a repeat set, and could have further reduced the deficit but for Hall's foot straying into touch as he flicked the ball back for Jowitt to go over.

The visitors' hopes were finally dashed when a spill from Mike McMeeken sent Jai Field scurrying the length of the field to score Wigan's fourth. A late effort from Wakefield's Ky Rodwell made the final scoreline more respectable.

Wakefield head coach Daryl Powell criticised the officials, saying: "I do think the refereeing department have to ask themselves a couple of questions.

"There's two teams that were top class but there's other parts of the game that weren't. I'll be asking my team to get better from tonight and I think [the officials] should be doing the same."

Leopards continue play-off charge with emphatic rout

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Leigh Leopards against Bradford Bulls in the Super League

Leigh Leopards continued their charge for the play-offs with a 62-10 thumping of Bradford Bulls.

Adam Cook scored 30 points, slotting over all 11 kicks and crossing for two tries, with Leigh adding 48 points in a one-sided second half.

Robbie Mulhern scored the first try for the hosts in the 12th minute, with Cook adding the conversion and a penalty before poor handling by the Leopards led to Waqa Blake powering over in the corner for Bradford.

Louis Brogan ended a spell of Leigh pressure by scoring their second try to make it 14-4 at the break, and the tone for the second half was set from the opening moment.

Bradford fumbled the kick-off, allowing Innes Senior to go over in the corner, and the tries arrived thick and fast for the hosts.

Lachlan Lam started and finished a move in the 48th minute before playing in Cook, who chased down his own kick.

Senior then grabbed his second, Umyla Hanley finished off Lam's brilliant long pass and Joe Ofahengaue completed a flowing move with more than 10 minutes still remaining.

Cook then broke away for his second try and Lam finished off a brilliant individual performance with his second, although the final word went to Bradford and Eliot Peposhi.
